data.name: Manaranjan
data.gender_notes: Manaranjan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manaranjan is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'manas' (mind) and 'rajas' (passion). This name signifies the one who is the embodiment of the juice of the mind and passion. In Hindu mythology, Manaranjan is also known as the name of the divine nectar Amrita, which was churned from the ocean of milk by the gods and demons to attain immortality.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of the divine nectar of the mind and passion
data.etymology: Manaranjan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Juice of manasa (mind) and rajas (passion).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manaranjan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Manaranjan is indicative of the rich cultural heritage and mythology of Hinduism. It is not only a beautiful name, but also one with deep meaning and significance. The usage of Sanskrit words in the name reflects the importance of the language in Hinduism and the influence it has had on Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Manaranjan lies in its connection to the divine nectar Amrita. As mentioned in Hindu mythology, the gods and demons churned the ocean of milk to obtain this elixir of immortality. The name Manaranjan, derived from the words 'manas' (mind) and 'rajas' (passion), represents the idea that just as the gods and demons sought the immortality of Amrita, the human mind is also in constant pursuit of knowledge and wisdom, which can lead to spiritual growth and enlightenment. Furthermore, the name can also be seen as a reminder to keep our passions and desires under control, as they can lead us towards spiritual growth or destruction, much like the events of the churning of the ocean of milk.
